claims.statement: Allocation rule v18 (deployed 22:00, east-node-first reservation for multi-node orders) introduced a defect that flags split-reservation exceptions, causing carriers to reject or not see the pickup orders.
claims.corroboration: m8_e03 confirms v18 live at 22:00; m8_e10 shows split-reservation exception flag on every held order; m8_e02 shows only east node affected and timing aligns (06:00 onset ~8 hours after deployment). m8_e01 notes allocation totals reconcile, ruling out gross inventory error.
claims.limitation: Split-reservation exceptions do not inherently mean a rule defect; they could be correct flags for a downstream carrier feed lag or dock capacity issue.

claims.statement: East node carrier feed (integration or pickup scheduling) is lagged or disconnected; carriers booked the pickup but the feed did not process the confirmation, so orders remain in 'awaiting pickup' state.
claims.corroboration: m8_e02 isolates issue to east-node lanes; m8_e09 notes observability gap (dashboards cannot see carrier-side confirmation vs booked state); m8_e01 carrier ops reports no obvious dock issue but cannot see cross-system reconciliation.
claims.limitation: Carrier ops on-call did not immediately spot a lag; would need partition offset or carrier confirmation audit to verify.

claims.statement: East node dock capacity reached saturation; allocation system booked pickups but carriers cannot stage more orders, causing a backlog in 'awaiting pickup' state.
claims.corroboration: m8_e02 shows 9% of overnight allocations held on east node; m8_e01 notes carrier ops found 'nothing obvious' on dock schedule, but did not quantify available slots vs pending orders.
claims.limitation: Stale evidence; a current dock capacity check would be needed to rule this in/out.

claims.statement: Allocation rule v18 created split-reservation exceptions (scope EXC-0921). All 186 held orders are in this scope. The split-reservation flag may itself be blocking carrier pickup, or the flag may be incidental and the issue is an independent east-node feed/capacity problem.
claims.corroboration: m8_r_exceptions confirms 100% of held orders are in EXC-0921 (rule v18 split-reservation scope); m8_e03 documents rule deployed 22:00; m8_e10 confirms split-reservation flag on all held orders; m8_e02 shows timing/isolation to east node.
claims.limitation: m8_r_exceptions limitation: cannot separate rule defect effect from east-node lanes effect since only rule-affected orders were routed there. Carrier confirmation needed to determine if split-reservation flag itself blocks pickup.

claims.statement: Carrier partition 2 (east-node) pickup-window feed consumer stopped advancing at 05:58. Allocation system correctly processed rule-v18 split reservations and booked pickups, but the lagged feed never sent notifications to carriers, causing 186 orders to remain awaiting pickup while carriers see no such bookings.
claims.corroboration: m8_r_offsets (tier-1, discriminating) shows partition 2 stopped at 05:58, 47+ min behind; m8_e02 shows orders began holding at 06:00 on east-node lanes only; m8_r_exceptions confirms all held orders are rule-v18-routed to east node (EXC-0921 scope); m8_e03 confirms rule change was at 22:00 (well before feed failure); m8_r_owner confirms reversible corrections exist.
claims.limitation: No direct evidence of what caused the feed consumer to stop (could be crash, queue full, downstream service down). But the feed lag is the sufficient explanation for the symptom (orders stuck, carriers unaware).

evidence.content:
07:12 Fulfilment lead: 186 orders allocated overnight to the east node are sitting 'allocated, awaiting pickup' and carriers are not collecting them.
07:20 Inventory control: allocation totals reconcile; nothing looks wrong on our side.
07:26 Security: no emergency overrides without approval.
07:31 Carrier ops on-call: looking at the dock schedule; nothing obvious.

The pickup-window feed consumer for carrier partition 2 (east-node carriers) stopped advancing at 05:58 and is 47 minutes behind and growing; partitions 0 and 1 are current. Slots for partition 2 are therefore booked against yesterday's carrier availability.
Dashboards count orders by state only. They do not show how a booked pickup relates to the carrier's own confirmation, and Inventory Control cannot see carrier-side records.

Carrier Operations confirms that any correction they apply is reversible and limited to a single carrier feed, and must run only after the affected feed and its lag are identified. Replaying held allocations is safe only after their pickup slots have been corrected.

Pickup slots for the affected carrier feed were realigned to current carrier availability; new bookings are confirmed inside their slots. Held orders stay held until their allocation windows are replayed. Reversible.
Orders held in 'allocated, awaiting pickup' for more than 90 minutes reached 9% of overnight allocations from 06:00, all on east-node lanes. Other nodes normal. The alert cannot attribute a cause.
